about: Co-op (The Co-operative Group) is a UK consumer co-operative running Co-op Food convenience stores (about 2,300), funeral care, insurance, legal services and wholesale supply, owned by millions of members. Revenue near 11 billion pounds. Headquartered in Manchester; origins in the 1844 Rochdale Pioneers. Not listed. Strong UK consumer brand, known for ethical positioning, and a sponsor of sports and community events.

FINN is a German car subscription provider where customers get a new or used car with insurance, registration and maintenance included for a monthly fee, fully online, with cars delivered to the door. Headquartered in Munich; founded 2019. Raised funding from investors such as BMW iVentures, with an operational scale in the tens of thousands of cars. Consumer-facing brand with growing awareness in Germany.

about: Kavak is a Mexican online used-car platform that buys, inspects, refurbishes and sells cars with financing and warranty, expanded to Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia and the UAE. Headquartered in Mexico City; founded 2016. Became Latin America's first car unicorn, raising funding from SoftBank, General Atlantic and others, valued at 8.7 billion dollars in 2022. Private. Strong consumer brand in Mexico and active in football sponsorship.

Meesho is an Indian e-commerce marketplace aimed at small and resellers, selling fashion, home goods and other low-priced products from sellers to tier-2 and tier-3 city shoppers with no seller commission model. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2015. Backed by SoftBank, Prosus and Fidelity, and listed on the NSE and BSE (MEESHO) after a December 2025 IPO. Mass-market consumer app with heavy cricket advertising.

Udaan is an Indian business-to-business e-commerce platform linking retailers and small shops with manufacturers and wholesalers across categories such as staples, FMCG, electronics, lifestyle and pharma, including Udaan's financing and logistics. Headquartered in Bengaluru; founded 2016 by former Flipkart executives. Raised over 1 billion dollars from Lightspeed, DST Global, Tencent and others at a 3.1 billion dollar valuation. Privately held. B2B marketplace without consumer visibility.

Amazon Seller Services is the Indian entity of Amazon that operates the Amazon.in online marketplace, connecting millions of third-party sellers with Indian shoppers and providing logistics, payments and advertising services. It earns commissions, fulfilment and ad fees. Based in Bengaluru, it is a wholly owned subsidiary of Amazon.com, which has committed billions of dollars to India. The consumer brand Amazon is hugely visible in India, and the company advertises and sponsors heavily, including cricket.

Faire is a San Francisco online wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with small and mid-sized brands, offering ordering, payment terms and shipping. Retailers in North America, Europe and beyond buy gifts, home goods, apparel and food from hundreds of thousands of brands, and Faire earns commissions and fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised over $1.7bn and was valued at about $12.4bn in 2022. Private. B2B marketplace, well known among independent shop owners but not to the general public.

PetSmart is the largest US pet specialty retailer, based in Phoenix, Arizona, with about 1,650 stores in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico plus e-commerce. It sells pet food, supplies and accessories, and provides grooming, training, boarding (PetsHotel), in-store Banfield veterinary clinics and adoption events. Revenue is around $10bn. Owned by private equity firm BC Partners since 2015. Private, with funding mainly debt and equity from sponsors. Strong US consumer brand with mass-market advertising.

PharmEasy is a Mumbai-based Indian online pharmacy and health platform, offering medicine delivery, diagnostic tests, teleconsultation and wholesale pharmacy supply through its owner API Holdings. It serves millions of Indian consumers and pharmacies, and has raised funds from Temasek, Prosus, TPG and others, with valuation falling sharply since a 2021 peak. In 2025 it undertook a major recapitalisation. Private. Notable consumer health brand in India, with advertising presence including cricket-linked campaigns.

US Foods is a Rosemont, Illinois foodservice distributor, supplying restaurants, hospitals, schools, hotels and other customers with food and supplies from about 70 distribution centres. It sells fresh and frozen products, plus private-label lines such as Chef's Store cash-and-carry, with revenue around $38bn and about 30,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (USFD). B2B, with little consumer awareness, though its trucks are widely seen in the US; it has used sports sponsorship such as stadium partnerships.

Carro is a Singapore-headquartered online used car marketplace and automotive platform operating in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong and Taiwan, combining car sales, financing, insurance, subscriptions and an auction business. Founded in 2012, it became a unicorn in 2021 and has raised over $1.1bn including debt, with backers like SoftBank and Temasek. Private. Strong consumer brand in Singapore and nearby markets, with significant marketing spend.

inKind is an Austin, Texas fintech that gives diners rewards and financing for dining out, working with restaurants to offer credit to spend at their venues and rewards in return, run through the inKind app. Restaurants get working capital and marketing, and diners receive discounts. Launched in 2017, it has raised about $1.2bn including debt facilities, with investors such as Matrix Partners and Valar Ventures. Private. Known among US foodies and restaurateurs.

Marex is a London-based global commodities and financial markets services group (shown with a New York address), providing brokerage, clearing, hedging, market making and trading across energy, metals, agriculture and foreign exchange for corporates and institutions. Revenue is about $1.7bn. It listed on Nasdaq (MRX) in April 2024. B2B financial group with little consumer awareness, although it has made sponsorship moves in sport.

QVC is a Rocky Mount, North Carolina (corporate base West Chester, Pennsylvania) video and online retailer, selling home, fashion, beauty, jewellery and electronics through TV shopping channels and digital platforms in the US, UK, Germany, Japan and Italy. It is a subsidiary of Qurate Retail, and its sister brand HSN is also part of the group. Revenue runs near $10bn. Qurate is listed on Nasdaq (QRTEA). Well-known consumer shopping brand with an older, primarily female audience.

The Very Group is a Liverpool-based digital retailer and financial services company running the Very online store and the Littlewoods brand, selling fashion, homewares, electronics and toys on interest-bearing buy-now-pay-later credit to UK customers. Revenue is around GBP 2bn, with about 5 million active customers. Owned by the Barclay family trust, with Very Financial Services as a core earner. Private. Strong UK consumer brand with heavy advertising, and has sponsored football.

Vroom was a Houston, Texas online used car retailer that sold vehicles directly to consumers with delivery to the door. It shut its ecommerce used-vehicle business in early 2024 and is now focused on its UACC auto lending unit, and parts of the company went through a prepackaged Chapter 11 restructuring in late 2024. Listed on Nasdaq (VRM) before the changes. A formerly well-advertised consumer brand, now largely a wound-down consumer finance business.

Clearco is a Toronto fintech, formerly Clearbanc, that offers revenue-based financing to e-commerce and software companies, advancing cash for marketing and inventory in exchange for a share of future revenue. It restructured in 2022-23, cutting staff and exiting several markets. Funding of about $960m includes equity and debt. Private. B2B fintech known to online merchants, with no consumer brand awareness.

Vishal Mega Mart is an Indian value retail chain, based in Gurugram, running over 600 department-style stores in tier 2 and tier 3 cities selling apparel, general merchandise and fast-moving consumer goods, much of it under its own private labels. Serving middle- and lower-income households, it earns from retail sales and has an online channel. Controlled by Kedaara Capital and Partners Group (after Temasek's earlier ownership), it listed on the NSE and BSE in December 2024. Strong value-retail brand in India with modest national advertising.

Ferguson is a Newport News, Virginia (US-listed) wholesale distributor of plumbing, heating, HVAC, waterworks and building products, serving residential and commercial contractors in the US and Canada from over 1,700 locations. Revenue is about $30bn. Once part of Wolseley UK, it moved its primary listing to the NYSE (FERG) in 2022. B2B distributor, known to trade professionals, with low consumer awareness.

Ocado Group is a British online grocery technology company, based in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, which developed a robotic warehouse and fulfilment system licensed to grocers such as Kroger, Coles, Aeon and Sobeys, and runs the Ocado Retail UK online supermarket with Marks and Spencer. Revenue from technology fees and retail is over GBP 3bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (OCDO). Ocado is a well-known UK consumer brand, though its technology business is B2B.

Flipkart is a Bengaluru-based Indian e-commerce marketplace, selling electronics, fashion, home goods and groceries, and also operating Myntra, Cleartrip and PhonePe previously, to hundreds of millions of customers. Walmart bought a majority stake in 2018 for about $16bn. Funding shown is about $15bn. Private, with a planned IPO. Among India's best-known consumer brands, with heavy advertising and its Big Billion Days sale, plus cricket sponsorship.

Diebold Nixdorf is a North Canton, Ohio supplier of ATMs, self-checkout, point-of-sale systems and related software and services to banks and retailers worldwide, with roughly 20,000 employees and revenue near $3.7bn. It restructured through a Chapter 11 filing in 2023 and emerged with debt reduced, relisting on the NYSE (DBD). B2B equipment brand, the ATMs are widely seen though consumers seldom know the brand.

Viacom18 Digital Ventures (JioCinema's holding entity) was the Indian streaming and digital media company, based in Mumbai, a joint venture between Reliance Industries' Viacom18 and Bodhi Tree Systems (James Murdoch and Uday Shankar), which ran JioCinema, streaming IPL and other sports rights. It merged with Disney Star in 2024 to form JioStar, creating Jio Hotstar. Funding of INR 204bn reflects Bodhi Tree's investment. Now part of JioStar, one of India's biggest media brands.

about: Vinted is a Lithuanian online marketplace for second-hand fashion, based in Vilnius, where individuals buy and sell clothes, shoes and accessories, with buyers paying a protection fee. It has over 100 million registered members in about 20 markets across Europe and the US, and reported revenue of around EUR 800m. Valued at EUR 5bn in a 2024 secondary sale. Private, backed by Insight and Accel. Strong consumer brand across Europe, with large advertising spending.

Clikalia is a Madrid-based Spanish proptech company that buys flats directly from owners, renovates them and sells them on, with an online process for quick offers, operating in Spain, Portugal and Italy. It makes money on property resale and financing, and has raised about EUR 1.1bn, including debt. Private. Consumer property brand with modest awareness in Spain, and some sports sponsorship.

Groupon is a Chicago online marketplace offering discounted deals on local services, travel, restaurants and goods to consumers, funded by merchants' commissions. Founded in 2008, it once had a $13bn market value but has since shrunk, with revenue under $500m, and shifted to a focus on local experiences. Listed on Nasdaq (GRPN). Widely recognised consumer brand from its early deal-of-the-day era, now much smaller.

Boots UK is a Nottingham-based British pharmacy and health and beauty retailer, with about 2,000 stores, selling prescriptions, medicines, cosmetics, toiletries and own-label products such as No7, Soap and Glory and Boots Own Brand, plus the Advantage Card loyalty scheme. It is owned by Walgreens Boots Alliance, which was taken private by Sycamore Partners in 2025. Private. Very strong UK high street consumer brand, with a history of sports partnerships.

Bukalapak is an Indonesian e-commerce company founded in 2010 in Jakarta, offering a marketplace connecting small merchants and consumers, plus Mitra Bukalapak, which serves small neighborhood stores. It listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (BUKA) in 2021 in the country's largest IPO, and now shifts toward online-to-offline and virtual products. Backed by Ant, Microsoft and Emtek. Well-known consumer brand in Indonesia, though smaller than Tokopedia and Shopee.

Bechtle is a Neckarsulm, Germany-based IT service provider and reseller, founded in 1983, serving public sector and business customers with hardware, software, cloud and managed services across Europe. Revenue is about 6 billion euros with over 14,000 employees. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (BC8, MDAX). The input lists funding of 750 million. B2B with limited consumer awareness, though it has sponsored football in Germany.

FEMSA is a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational and one of Latin America's largest beverage and retail groups. It owns about 47 percent of Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler, and operates OXXO, a chain of over 22,000 convenience stores, as well as pharmacy and fuel retail, and has held a stake in Heineken. Listed on the Mexican exchange and the NYSE (FMX). OXXO is a household brand across Latin America.

Settle is a US B2B cash-flow management and financial technology platform serving e-commerce and consumer brands, helping them manage payables, pay suppliers and access working capital. The input lists reported funding of about $761 million, most likely credit facilities. B2B fintech with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Autodoc is a Berlin-based online retailer of vehicle spare parts and accessories, founded in 2008 by Alexej Erdle, selling over a million parts to drivers and garages in more than 25 European countries via its own web shops. Revenue is over a billion euros. Reported funding of about 580 million euros; an IPO was planned but postponed in 2023. Consumer e-commerce brand with high awareness in Germany and Eastern Europe, with football and motorsport sponsorship.

TaoCheChe is a Chinese automotive e-commerce company, associated with the Alibaba ecosystem, that sells new cars online and offers car-related services to buyers, working with dealers and manufacturers. It is based in China (Shanghai). The input lists reported funding of about $591 million. Consumer-facing platform with moderate awareness in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: TaoCheChe is an innovative company focused on the field .

about: Seven & i Holdings is a Tokyo-based Japanese retail holding company, owner of 7-Eleven convenience stores (including 7-Eleven Inc. in North America with about 85,000 stores worldwide), Ito-Yokado supermarkets and Denny's Japan, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (3382). Founder-family and shareholders resisted Couche-Tard's takeover proposal in 2024-25, which was withdrawn. Revenue is over 11 trillion yen. Customers are consumers, with very high brand awareness globally.

Cazoo was a UK online used-car retailer founded in 2018 and headquartered in London that sold cars with home delivery and a seven-day return policy, and sponsored Everton FC and Aston Martin's F1 team. It listed on the NYSE through a SPAC in 2021 at a multi-billion dollar valuation but struggled with losses, and entered administration in 2024 after restructuring. Customers were UK consumers. Notable past sports sponsor, now defunct, so not an active prospect.

Bimbo Bakeries USA is the US subsidiary of Grupo Bimbo, the Mexican baked-goods multinational, headquartered in Horsham, Pennsylvania. It makes and distributes packaged bread, buns, cakes and snacks under brands such as Sara Lee, Thomas', Entenmann's, Ball Park, Arnold, Oroweat and Stroehmann through a direct-store delivery network and grocery retail, with about 22,000 employees. Parent company Bimbo is listed in Mexico. Mass consumer brand in US supermarkets, a known sports sponsor via Grupo Bimbo.

CARS24 is an Indian used-car platform headquartered in Gurugram, founded in 2015 by Vikram Chopra and others. It lets consumers sell cars through inspection and instant pricing, and buy certified used cars via online listings, with financing and insurance add-ons, and operated in the UAE and Australia before scaling back. Backed by SoftBank, Tiger Global and DST, it reached a valuation of about 3 billion dollars. Strong consumer brand in India, known for cricket sponsorships.

FlixBus is a European intercity bus brand headquartered in Munich that works on a network model: partner coach companies run buses under the green FlixBus branding while Flix handles routes, ticketing and marketing. It carries tens of millions of passengers across Europe and the US, since buying Greyhound in 2021, and also runs FlixTrain. Founded 2013. Parent Flix SE is owned by General Atlantic, Permira, Silver Lake and the founders. Strong consumer brand across Europe.

Toss is a South Korean mobile financial super app run by Viva Republica, headquartered in Seoul, providing payments, money transfer, a bank (Toss Bank), securities and credit scoring to well over 20 million users. Founded 2013 by Lee Seung-gun, it raised funding from global investors at a valuation reported above 7 billion dollars. Revenue includes fees, lending and brokerage. Very strong consumer brand in Korea with a heavy advertising presence.

Chewy is a US online pet retailer headquartered in Florida (Plantation/Dania Beach area) and listed on the NYSE (CHWY). It sells pet food, supplies and medications, runs a subscription Autoship programme and operates CarePlus vet clinics, serving about 20 million active customers with revenue near 11 billion dollars. Founded 2011, acquired by PetSmart in 2017 and floated in 2019; BC Partners remains a significant holder. Strong consumer brand known for customer service.

Xiaohongshu (RED, Little Red Book) is a Chinese social and lifestyle commerce platform headquartered in Shanghai, where users share product reviews, travel and beauty tips and shop within the app. It has over 300 million monthly active users, mostly young urban women, and earns from advertising, e-commerce and live streaming. Founded 2013 by Charlwyn Mao and Miranda Qu. Privately held with investors such as Alibaba and Tencent. Became widely discussed internationally in early 2025. Strong consumer brand for reaching young Chinese audiences.

Butternut Box is a London-based direct-to-consumer fresh dog food company that sells freshly cooked, vet-developed meals delivered frozen on subscription to UK dog owners. Founded 2016, it has raised significant venture and private equity funding, including from L Catterton. Revenue is subscription-based. Customers are UK pet owners. Growing consumer brand with strong online advertising presence in the UK. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Nuvemshop (Tiendanube) is a Latin American e-commerce platform based in Sao Paulo that lets merchants build and run online stores with payments, shipping and marketing tools, serving over 100,000 merchants in Brazil, Argentina, Mexico and other markets. Founded 2011, it has raised funding from Kaszek, Qualcomm Ventures and Tiger Global at a valuation above 3 billion dollars. Revenue comes from subscriptions and payments. B2B SaaS, well known among Latin American online sellers.

Carsome is a Malaysian online used-car marketplace headquartered in Petaling Jaya that lets consumers buy and sell inspected, certified cars with financing and insurance, and also provides B2B dealer auctions across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore. Founded 2015, it raised more than 400 million dollars from Temasek, Gaw Capital and others, achieving unicorn status in 2021. Customers are consumers and dealers. Strong consumer brand in Malaysia.

Oda is a Norwegian online grocery retailer headquartered in Oslo that delivers groceries to homes in Norway and Sweden from automated warehouses, formerly known as Kolonial.no. Founded 2013, it raised hundreds of millions of dollars from venture investors including Kinnevik and has scaled back international expansion to focus on Norway. Revenue is above 5 billion Norwegian kroner. Customers are urban households. Recognised consumer brand in Norway with sports and cultural partnerships.

Flutterwave is an African payments technology company that lets merchants accept card, bank transfer, mobile money and other payments, and offers payouts and cross-border infrastructure through its Flutterwave Store and APIs. Customers are businesses such as Uber and Booking.com operating in Africa. Founded in 2016 by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji and Olugbenga Agboola, with operations led from Lagos, Nigeria and listed in San Francisco. Valued around $3 billion at its 2022 round. Private. B2B brand with strong recognition in African tech.

The RealReal is an online luxury consignment marketplace that sells authenticated pre-owned designer goods: handbags, jewellery, watches, clothing and art. Consumers consign items and buyers purchase, with revenue from commissions and sales, supported by in-house authenticators and retail stores. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in San Francisco, with annual revenue near $600 million. Listed on Nasdaq (REAL). Well-known US luxury resale brand with an affluent customer base.

Camping World is the largest US retailer of recreational vehicles and camping products, operating Camping World and Gander Outdoors stores, RV dealerships, service centres, plus the Good Sam club and insurance services. Customers are RV buyers and campers. Headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois, with about 200 locations and revenue above $6 billion. Listed on NYSE (CWH), controlled by chairman and CEO Marcus Lemonis through ML Acquisition. Very recognisable US brand, and a known sports and NASCAR sponsor.

Metro Inc. is a Canadian food and pharmacy retailer based in Montreal, operating Metro, Super C, Food Basics and Adonis grocery stores plus Jean Coutu and Brunet pharmacies, with about 1,000 food stores and 650 pharmacies in Quebec and Ontario. Customers are consumers, with revenue of about C$21 billion. Listed on the TSX (MRU). Very strong regional consumer brand, a frequent sponsor in sport and community events in Quebec.

Petco is a US pet specialty retailer selling pet food, supplies and live animals, and providing grooming, training and veterinary services through Vetco clinics, with about 1,500 stores and an online business. Customers are pet owners, with revenue about $6 billion. Headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 1965. Listed on Nasdaq (WOOF) since 2021, after being owned by CVC Capital and CPP Investments. Strong consumer brand across the US, with stadium naming rights at Petco Park.

Chehaoduo is a Beijing-based Chinese online car trading group operating Guazi (used cars) and Maodou (new cars) platforms, connecting buyers and sellers directly and offering financing and services. Customers are Chinese car buyers and dealers. Backed by SoftBank, Hillhouse and others, with large past funding. Crunchbase shows about $3.8 billion in funding. Private. Scaled back its operations in recent years. Familiar in China through heavy advertising.

about: Suning.com is a Chinese retailer of electronics, appliances and general merchandise, operating thousands of physical stores and an online platform, logistics and financial services. Founded in 1990 and based in Nanjing, with revenue in the hundreds of billions of yuan at its peak. It ran into financial trouble in 2021 and was bailed out by a group of Jiangsu state-linked investors. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (002024). Its parent group owned Inter Milan until 2024 and has deep sports sponsorship experience. Strong Chinese consumer brand.

Hangzhou-based Chinese used-car platform (Souche), founded 2012 and backed by Alibaba, providing SaaS tools, financing and online sales for dealerships and consumers. Revenue comes from dealer software and transaction fees. Strong B2B presence in China with limited consumer awareness, and none outside China. Souche was one of the early online used car marketplaces in China, and works with thousands of dealers.

US home goods retailer whose brand was bought out of bankruptcy by Overstock.com in 2023 (Overstock then renamed itself Bed Bath & Beyond Inc.), shifting to an online-first model with a few stores. Sells furniture, bedding, kitchenware and decor to US consumers. Based in Murray, Utah; listed on the NYSE (BBBY). Famous legacy consumer brand name in the US, though a much smaller business now.

Paris-based marketplace software company, founded 2012, powering enterprise marketplaces and drop-ship platforms for retailers and B2B sellers such as Carrefour, Best Buy and Leroy Merlin. Valued at about $3.5 billion in 2022. B2B brand, with some visibility in retail technology. Privately held. Mirakl sells to enterprises on a subscription model. Mirakl has hundreds of enterprise customers, including retailers across Europe and North America.

Amazon's online payment service, based in Seattle, letting shoppers use their Amazon account to pay at third-party websites and apps. Revenue comes from merchant fees. As part of Amazon, brand visibility is high among consumers where it is accepted. Standalone company funding figure in the input is not meaningful. Amazon Pay is available in the US, UK, EU and India and is used by hundreds of thousands of merchants.

British frozen food retailer, founded 1970 in Oswestry, with about 1,000 stores in the UK and online, owned by Iceland Foods Group. Customers are UK shoppers. Revenue about GBP 3.5 billion. Strong consumer brand recognised through advertising and sponsorship. Operates frozen food stores plus home delivery, and is known for its Christmas advertising campaigns. Privately owned, with Malcolm Walker as founder.

Paris-based online marketplace for pre-owned luxury fashion, founded 2009, with more than 30 million members worldwide. Valued at about $1.7 billion in 2022. Consumer brand with strong awareness among fashion buyers. Operates in about 40 countries, earning commission on sales and verifying authenticity of items. Strong brand among fashion resale buyers. The company was founded in 2009 and is based in Paris and has offices in New York and London.

Plano, Texas-based beauty retail and distribution company, founded 1964, with about 5,000 stores selling Sally Beauty and CosmoProf hair and nail products. Listed on the NYSE (SBH). Known US consumer retailer. Customers are professional stylists and consumers, with stores in the US and Europe. Moderate consumer awareness. Sally Beauty has about 30,000 employees and operates the Sally Beauty Supply and Beauty Systems Group chains selling to professional salons and individual shoppers.

Helsinki-based Finnish landlord, founded 1938 and owned by pension funds and the City of Helsinki, renting about 28,000 apartments. Regional consumer brand. Operates in Finland and the Baltics, with a loyal tenant base. Regional brand. SATO is owned by Finnish pension funds and the City of Helsinki and manages tens of thousands of apartments. Customers are tenants. Consumer-facing in Finland, no international profile.

Minneapolis-based buy now pay later fintech, founded 2016, serving US consumers and merchants, listed on Nasdaq (SEZL). Consumer brand. Customers are consumers and online merchants, earning merchant fees and subscriptions. Strong awareness among younger US shoppers. Listed on Nasdaq (SEZL). Founded in Minneapolis in 2016; users split purchases into instalments with no interest. Strong awareness among younger US shoppers and active in sponsorship.

Toronto-based online used-car retailer, founded 2016, selling pre-owned cars to Canadian consumers via a website with home delivery, financing and trade-in, and through its marketing. Customers are individual car buyers. Raised about $437 million. Consumer brand with strong visibility in Canada. Revenue is vehicle sales margin and financing. Clutch buys vehicles at auction and from owners, refurbishes them, and sells them with a limited warranty and a return window, using its own logistics network.

Knave is a Paris-based technology company listed in mobile apps and retail technology, offering design and management tools for retail activity per the input. The funding figure shown (348.5 million) is large for an unknown firm and may include other capital. Funding of 348.5 million is shown, but the input does not identify any retail customers, apps or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Morrisons (Wm Morrison Supermarkets) is a UK supermarket chain with around 500 stores, one of the big four grocers, based in Bradford, West Yorkshire. It is unusually vertically integrated, owning food manufacturing sites and supplying wholesale customers including Amazon and McColl's. Founded in 1899 and listed until 2021, it was taken private by US private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice in a deal worth about 10 billion pounds. Revenue is roughly 17 billion pounds with about 100,000 staff. Very high consumer visibility across the UK, with no presence outside it.

Symbotic provides AI-enabled warehouse automation: robotic storage and retrieval systems that palletise and move cases for large retailers and distributors. Its largest customer is Walmart, which also owns a stake and supported its listing; other customers include Target, Albertsons and C&S Wholesale Grocers. Based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, it went public via a SPAC merger with SVF Investment Corp. in 2022 and trades on Nasdaq (SYM). Revenue exceeds 2 billion dollars. In 2025 it agreed to acquire Walmart's robotics unit. B2B technology with little public brand awareness.

MatHem is a Swedish online grocery retailer delivering food and household products to homes in Stockholm, Gothenburg, Malmo and elsewhere in Sweden, with a mix of own-brand and supplier products. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Stockholm, it was taken over by Swedish rival Axfood and merged it into Axfood's online business. Funding shown is about 510 million dollars. Known across Swedish consumers, with a recognisable delivery fleet, but only in Sweden.

Celero Commerce is a Nashville payments and commerce technology company providing integrated payment processing, point-of-sale software and merchant services to small and mid-sized businesses, including restaurants, retailers and healthcare practices, through sales partners and software vendors. It earns processing fees and software subscriptions. Funding shown is about 375 million dollars. B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

about: Savers Value Village is a for-profit thrift retailer with over 300 stores in the United States, Canada and Australia, operating as Savers, Value Village, Unique Thrift and Village des Valeurs. It sells second-hand clothing, accessories and household goods, sourced mainly from donations collected through paid partnerships with non-profit organisations. Based in Bellevue, Washington, it is controlled by Ares Management and listed on the NYSE (SVV) since 2023. Revenue is about 1.5 billion dollars. Strong recognition among North American thrift shoppers.

BarkBox (BARK, Inc.) is a US pet products company that sells monthly BarkBox toy and treat subscriptions, Super Chewer boxes for heavy chewers and BarkBox Dental, along with the Bark Eats and Bark Supplies lines for the retail market. Based in New York with a distribution base in Ohio, it listed on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in 2021 and has revenue of about 450 million dollars. Customers are dog owners; subscription and e-commerce sales. Recognisable consumer brand among US pet owners.

RealTruck is a Michigan-based maker and online retailer of truck and Jeep accessories, including tonneau covers (Bak, Retrax), running boards (Go Rhino), bed liners and lighting, and operates e-commerce sites such as RealTruck.com and Truck Hero. Customers are pickup and SUV owners buying online. Based in Ann Arbor with manufacturing across North America, it is owned by private equity firms including Leonard Green and Partners, and includes brands like Extang. Strong among US truck enthusiasts, with some motorsport and off-road sponsorships.

Scan.com is a London-based online marketplace for diagnostic imaging, letting patients and doctors book MRI, CT and ultrasound scans at partner clinics across the UK with reports delivered online. It sells to private patients, insurers and employers, earning a margin on each scan. Funding shown is about 287 million dollars, including debt. Modest consumer awareness in the UK private healthcare sector.

about: Zoomcar is a Bengaluru-based car-sharing marketplace in India and emerging markets, connecting car owners with renters who drive themselves, with hosts earning rental income. Founded in 2013, it also operates in Egypt, Indonesia and Vietnam, and listed on Nasdaq (ZCAR) in 2023 via a SPAC merger with Innovative International Acquisition Corp. Customers are urban Indian consumers and travellers. Moderate consumer awareness in India, with a small revenue base and losses.

Coppel is a Mexican retailer headquartered in Culiacan, Sinaloa, founded in 1941, with over 1,000 stores selling furniture, appliances, electronics, clothing and financial services such as credit, savings and a bank, Bancoppel. It sells mostly on store credit to lower and middle-income Mexican consumers, and also operates online. Family-owned, with tens of thousands of employees and revenue in the billions of dollars. Very high consumer recognition in Mexico and a sponsor in Mexican sport, with presence in the United States too.

Cencosud is a Chilean multinational retailer, based in Santiago, operating supermarkets (Jumbo, Santa Isabel, Disco, Wong), the Paris department stores, Easy home improvement, shopping centres (Costanera Center) and financial services across Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and Colombia, plus the US via The Fresh Market. Listed on the Santiago Stock Exchange (CENCOSUD), with revenue of over 15 billion dollars. Very strong consumer brands across Latin America.

Jushi Holdings is a US multi-state cannabis operator based in Boca Raton, Florida, running medical and adult-use dispensaries under the Beyond/Hello, The Bank and Nature's Remedy names in Pennsylvania, Illinois, Virginia, Nevada and elsewhere, and producing branded cannabis products. Listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (JUSH). Customers are cannabis consumers and patients. Regional retail brands, and cannabis marketing restrictions generally limit sponsorship.

dLocal is a Montevideo-based payments company that lets global merchants such as Amazon, Spotify and Uber accept local payment methods and make payouts in emerging markets across Latin America, Africa and Asia. Founded in 2016, it listed on Nasdaq (DLO) in 2021, processing tens of billions of dollars a year. B2B payments infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

QVC Group (formerly Qurate Retail) is a US video and online commerce group, headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, operating the QVC and HSN television shopping networks, Zulily and Cornerstone brands such as Ballard Designs and Frontgate. It sells home, fashion, beauty and jewellery to consumers through TV, web and apps. Listed on Nasdaq (QVCGA). Revenue has declined to around 10 billion dollars. Well known in the US among home shoppers.

WHSmith is a British retailer, historically known for its high street stores, newspapers, stationery and books. It sold its high street chain in 2025 to Modella Capital and now operates as a travel retailer, with stores in airports, railway stations, hospitals and motorway services in the UK, North America, Australia and elsewhere. Based in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange (SMWH), founded in 1792. Very high UK consumer recognition.

PDD Holdings is the parent of Pinduoduo, the Chinese social e-commerce marketplace, and Temu, its international shopping platform launched in 2022 which sells low-priced goods across the US, Europe and other markets. Temu is a heavy advertiser, including a major Super Bowl presence, so it has strong consumer visibility.

JD Health is a Chinese online healthcare platform, a subsidiary of JD.com based in Beijing and listed in Hong Kong (6618), which sells prescription and over-the-counter drugs, health products and offers online consultations and family doctor services to consumers across China. Revenue is about 60 billion yuan a year, mainly from product sales and advertising. Consumers use it through the JD app. Strong consumer brand in China via JD.

eBay is a San Jose, California online marketplace, founded in 1995 and listed on Nasdaq (EBAY), where consumers and businesses buy and sell new and used goods, from cars parts to collectibles, via auctions and fixed-price listings. It earns fees and advertising, with about $10 billion in revenue and over 130 million active buyers. Operating in dozens of countries, it is a globally recognised consumer brand and has previously sponsored sport.

Tuniu is a Nanjing-based Chinese online leisure travel company, founded in 2006 and listed on Nasdaq (TOUR), selling package tours, hotels, flights and cruises to Chinese consumers, with a focus on organised group and self-guided trips. It earns commissions and package margins. Revenue has been a few hundred million yuan. It has a recognised consumer brand in China, but a smaller scale than Trip.com.

FirstCry is an Indian online and offline retailer of baby, kids and maternity products, headquartered in Pune, and operated by Brainbees Solutions. It sells clothing, toys, diapers and gear through a website, app and several hundred stores, and has home brands such as Babyhug. Listed on the NSE and BSE in August 2024. Backed by SoftBank, Premji Invest and Mahindra. Strong brand among Indian parents.

Uzum is an Uzbekistan-based digital ecosystem, headquartered in Tashkent, operating the Uzum Market e-commerce platform, Uzum Bank digital banking and Uzum Nasiya instalment services, plus fast delivery and fintech. It became Uzbekistan's first unicorn in 2024, and funding shown is about $465 million. Strong consumer brand across the country.
